title: Indian Contract Act, 1872 — Section 201 (Termination of agency)

content.overview: An agency is terminated by the principal revoking his authority; or by the agent renouncing the business of the agency; or by the business of the agency being completed; or by either the principal or agent dying or becoming of unsound mind; or by the principal being adjudicated an insolvent under the provisions of any Act for the time being in force for the relief of insolvent debtors.
content.glance: Agency ends by: revocation; renunciation; completion of business; death or unsound mind of either; insolvency of principal.
content.study: An agency is terminated by the principal revoking his authority; or by the agent renouncing the business of the agency; or by the business of the agency being completed; or by either the principal or agent dying or becoming of unsound mind; or by the principal being adjudicated an insolvent under the provisions of any Act for the time being in force for the relief of insolvent debtors. Read with ss. 202–210 on coupled interest, revocation limits, notice and when termination takes effect.

sections.heading: Renunciation by agent
sections.body: Agent renounces the business of the agency.

sections.heading: Completion of business
sections.body: Business of the agency is completed.

sections.heading: Death or unsound mind
sections.body: Either principal or agent dies or becomes of unsound mind.

sections.heading: Insolvency of principal
sections.body: Principal adjudicated insolvent under applicable insolvency law.

examples.title: Application of Section 201
examples.body: Facts that satisfy the elements stated in the statutory text of Section 201 produce the consequence described in that section. Do not add elements beyond the text.

hypotheticals.question: Do the facts engage Section 201?
hypotheticals.analysis: Compare the facts with the statutory elements in Section 201. If they match, the statutory consequence follows; otherwise it does not.

questionsAndAnswers.question: How should a Section 201 problem be analysed?
questionsAndAnswers.answer: Identify the terminating event among the five statutory modes; then apply ss. 202–210 for limits and consequences.

examTips: List all five modes of termination.
